data.content_ref: inline:Compute the grounded extension lazily for a target conjecture: expand only the subgraph reachable by attack and defense edges up to the first fixpoint hit, memoize labels of visited nodes, and certify the result by a polynomial check that no omitted node can reach the target through an undefeated attacker path. This changes the cost profile (potentially sub-linear in practice) while keeping worst-case polynomial, and moves the determinism guarantee from the full-graph fixed point to a fixed traversal order. The criticizable claim is that the certification check is itself a fixed-point computation in disguise, so the 'lazy' version may merely re-derive the full extension in the worst case and add bookkeeping without a semantic strengthening.
